name: Decline Crunch
summary: An abdominal exercise performed on a decline bench that isolates spinal flexion against gravity.

setup: Adjust a decline bench to the desired angle and secure your lower legs snugly beneath the padded rollers.
Lie back with your head lower than your hips, resting your back fully on the pad.
Cross your arms across your chest or place your fingertips lightly beside your temples without interlacing your fingers behind your head.
steps: Contract your abdominals to curl your ribcage toward your pelvis, lifting your head and shoulder blades off the bench.
Pause at the top of the movement for a brief contraction, keeping tension on your abdominal wall.
Lower your torso back down in a slow, controlled eccentric motion until your shoulder blades touch the pad, then immediately begin the next repetition without resting.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you curl your torso upward against gravity; inhale smoothly as you lower your body down.
cues: Roll your ribs toward your belt buckle

common_faults.fault: Swinging the upper body up using hip flexor momentum rather than abdominal contraction.
common_faults.correction: Focus on curling the spine vertebrae by vertebrae and keep your lower back in contact with or close to the pad.

common_faults.fault: Pulling on the back of the neck with the hands.
common_faults.correction: Cross your arms across your chest or keep your fingertips gently touching your ears.

common_faults.fault: Dropping quickly on the eccentric phase without muscular tension.
common_faults.correction: Resist gravity on the way down, taking two to three seconds to return to the starting position.

precautions: Ensure the decline bench leg-catch rollers are fully locked and securely pinned before lying back.
